=== no such task
orchestrator: update_task {"id":"T09","title":"x"}
refusal:
there is no task 'T09' (the run has tasks T01 to T06)

=== no id
orchestrator: update_task {"title":"x"}
refusal:
there is no task '' (the run has tasks T01 to T06)

=== a done task
orchestrator: update_task {"id":"T01","title":"Read it again"}
refusal:
T01 is done and final. Add a task that depends on it instead.

=== a task that is being merged
orchestrator: update_task {"id":"T02","title":"Build it better"}
refusal:
T02 has finished and is being merged; it can no longer be changed. Add a task that depends on it instead.

=== a running task
orchestrator: update_task {"id":"T05","title":"Port all the tests"}
refusal:
T05 is running. Cancel it first if it must change, then retry it.

=== nothing to change
orchestrator: update_task {"id":"T06"}
refusal:
nothing to change: give title, brief, kind, writes, tier, tier_reason, depends_on or needs_report

=== it already is as described
orchestrator: update_task {"id":"T06","title":"Clean  up","kind":"implement","writes":true,"depends_on":["T02"],"brief":"Read the old importer and write down what it does, step by step, with the files it touches."}
refusal:
T06 already is as you describe it

=== the title is empty
orchestrator: update_task {"id":"T06","title":""}
refusal:
the title is empty

=== the brief is too short
orchestrator: update_task {"id":"T06","brief":"Tidy."}
refusal:
the brief is too short to work from: its agent knows nothing but the brief

=== it cannot depend on itself
orchestrator: update_task {"id":"T06","depends_on":["T06"]}
refusal:
T06 cannot depend on itself

=== a dependency cycle
orchestrator: update_task {"id":"T03","depends_on":["T04"]}
refusal:
that would make a dependency cycle: T03 -> T04 -> T03

=== depends_on names tasks that do not exist
orchestrator: update_task {"id":"T06","depends_on":["T02","T77"]}
refusal:
depends_on names tasks that do not exist: T77

=== the tier is none of the three
orchestrator: update_task {"id":"T06","tier":"cheap"}
refusal:
tier must be one of deep, standard, light

=== the tier's reason is empty
orchestrator: update_task {"id":"T06","tier_reason":""}
refusal:
tier_reason is empty: say in a sentence why this tier is enough for the task

=== needs_report is not a list
orchestrator: update_task {"id":"T06","needs_report":"T02"}
refusal:
needs_report must be a list of task ids

=== needs_report names a task it does not depend on
orchestrator: update_task {"id":"T06","needs_report":["T02","T01"]}
refusal:
needs_report names tasks this one does not depend on: T01. Add them to depends_on as well.

=== updated: a waiting task
orchestrator: update_task {"id":"T06","title":"Clean up the old importer","brief":"Remove the old importer once the new one is merged, with its tests and its fixtures.","depends_on":["T02","T05"]}
answer:
Updated T06 (title, brief, depends_on).

=== updated: a failed task
orchestrator: update_task {"id":"T03","brief":"Measure the old importer on the fixture files under testdata/, three runs each, and report the times."}
answer:
Updated T03 (brief). It is failed: call retry_task to queue it again.

=== updated: it depends on a failed task
orchestrator: update_task {"id":"T04","kind":"Writing"}
answer:
Updated T04 (kind). Note: it depends on T03 (failed) and will not start until that is retried and done, or the dependency is removed.

=== updated by a chat
chat: update_task {"id":"T04","title":"Write the migration guide","writes":true}
answer:
Updated T04 (title, writes). Note: it depends on T03 (failed) and will not start until that is retried and done, or the dependency is removed.

=== refused for a chat
chat: update_task {"id":"T01","title":"x"}
refusal:
T01 is done and final. Add a task that depends on it instead.

=== updated: the tier of a waiting task, and the reports it is given
orchestrator: update_task {"id":"T06","tier":"light","tier_reason":"It follows a recipe.","needs_report":["T05","T02"]}
answer:
Updated T06 (tier, tier_reason, needs_report).

=== updated: it no longer depends on a task whose report it was given
orchestrator: update_task {"id":"T06","depends_on":["T02"]}
answer:
Updated T06 (depends_on, needs_report).

=== updated: the tier of a failed task
orchestrator: update_task {"id":"T03","tier":"deep"}
answer:
Updated T03 (tier). It is failed: call retry_task to queue it again.

=== the notes gate
orchestrator: update_task {"id":"T01","writes":true}
refusal:
The notes are empty, so a task that changes files is refused. First record with set_notes what the goal requires, what done means and how it will be checked, and the approach the facts support. If you cannot write that yet, the run needs tasks that investigate (writes: false) before tasks that build.

=== the notes gate, a chat
chat: update_task {"id":"T01","writes":true}
refusal:
The run's notes are empty, so a task that changes files is refused: the orchestrator has not yet recorded what done means. Add a task that investigates (writes: false), or tell the orchestrator what the person wants.
